findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. 

The soda gun in the bar area was observed with tape holding the nozzle to the rest of the equipment. When asked, the PIC indicated that the item was damaged. The inspector stated that it needs to be repaired prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure that all equipment is maintained in a safe and proper repair at all times.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

An employee was observed to wash their hands and then use their bare hands to turn off the faucet, recontaminating the hands in the process. Education was conducted with the PIC and they are instructed to refresh hand washing procedures with staff. Ensure proper hand washing takes place at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The deflector shield of the ice machine in the bar area has slime build up observed. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean/sanitize and maintain clean/sanitized moving forward. The item was cleaned to correct.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.citation_text:
7-102.11 Common Name. Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

The bleach buckets in the kithcen are without labels and are the same type of buckets used for battering wash water and ice bath containers for foods. The PIC was notified and instructed to ensure that chemical containers are labeled so that they are not mixed up with food containers. Labels were added by an employee to correct the violation.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-102.11: Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. 

The two sani buckets in the kitchen are without labels. Chlorine bleach is used in the sanitizer and the buckets are the same type of container used for water at the batter station, that happens to be next to one of the buckets. The PIC was notified and added labels to the containers during this inspection to correct the violation.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  

An employee was observe to begin slicing a lemon for drinks without hand washing prior. Hand washing was discussed with the employee/PIC. Ensure that hand washing takes place prior to handling any RTE foods.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
3-202.15: FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. 

A can of chili sauce in the basement shelving is observed heavily dented. While discussing with the PIC they stated that they noticed it when putting away today’s truck, but hadn’t given it back to the company yet. Foods with damaged packaging should be stored separate from those intended for consumers until returned. The can was moved during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-202.12: (A) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be used according to LAW(C), Manufacturer’s directions (indicate for use in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT) (P).

The spray bottle used by the wait staff is observed to have bleached out the inspector’s test strips. Concentrations were discussed with the head waitress and PIC. The bottle was remade during the inspection to correct the violation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.13: (A) floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than 1mm (one thirty-second inch). (B) Floors in which water flush cleaning methods are used shall be provided with drains and be graded to drain. Floor and wall junctures shall be coved and SEALED.

Several inch gap is present between bar floor and bar wall under the 3 compartment sink where plumbing enters the floor. Close gap to prevent soil accumulation or ponding water.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
(REPEAT x3) : 6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.
The following areas need maintenance attention:
BAR: 1) seal triple sink to wall.
WAIT STATION: 1) cove base around garbage nook into ice bin nook is either missing, pulled from wall, or damaged. Replace cove base/trim around wait station.
KITCHEN: 1) caulk/cove wall to floor under the dish machine drainboard (gap is present); 
2) repair wall under triple sink and cove to floor (wall is currently bowing and appears to be water-damaged).

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
(REPEAT x3) 410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

Allergen certificate is only available for the kitchen manager at this time. Ensure that all CFPMs in the facility have passed an ANSI accredited allergen training and maintain copies of the certificates at the facility.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Employee observed to turn faucet off without the use of a barrier after washing hands. Employee observed to quickly rinse hands without cleaning hands for at least 20 seconds. CORRECTED- Inspector discussed with employee and PIC. Provided education.
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
Foods in the kitchen refrigerator freezer observed not fully frozen solid. Foods moved to chest freezer for storage. Adjust or repair unit to maintain frozen foods frozen.
3-501.11: Stored frozen FOODS shall be maintained frozen. [C]
